title: Finite-free termwise limit of a compatible finite-free complex tower
statement: Let R_n be commutative rings with surjective transitions phi_n and nilpotent kernels. Let A with compatible q_n:A→R_n satisfy the unique compatible-tuple universal property. Suppose P_n are complexes of finite-free R_n-modules, zero above one cutoff b, and u_n:P_(n+1)→P_n are semilinear surjective chain maps. Suppose the ordinary scalar-extension adjoints of u_n are chain isomorphisms theta_n. Then the termwise compatible-tuple limit is a bounded-above complex P of finite-free A-modules. Its projections p_n have the degreewise unique-compatible-tuple property, commute with u_n, and their ordinary scalar-extension adjoints are chain isomorphisms P tensor_A R_n→P_n.

proof.text: Restrict the varying-ring complexes along q_n to form a tower S of A-complexes, with the canonical restriction-composition comparison. Use the categorical degreewise limit complex and its literal projections. Forgetting to sets preserves limits, so its degree-i points have exactly the compatible-tuple existence-and-uniqueness property. The common upper bound passes to the limit because all degree-i terms above the bound are zero.

Apply the finite-free module tower inverse-limit theorem separately in each degree. It proves freeness and finiteness of the limit terms and invertibility of the ordinary scalar-extension adjoints of the projections. The ordinary adjunction on complexes makes these adjoints a chain map. A chain map invertible in each degree is an isomorphism, giving the required reduction chain isomorphisms. Its component adjunction identities are the desired projection equations.

theorem exists_finiteFree_complexTower_inverseLimit
    (R : ℕ → Type u) [∀ n, CommRing (R n)]
    (φ : ∀ n, R (n + 1) →+* R n)
    (hsurj : ∀ n, Function.Surjective (φ n))
    (hnil : ∀ n, IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (φ n)))
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (q : ∀ n, A →+* R n)
    (hq : ∀ n, q n = (φ n).comp (q (n + 1)))
    (hlim : ∀ x : ∀ n, R n, (∀ n, φ n (x (n + 1)) = x n) →
      ∃! a : A, ∀ n, q n a = x n)
    (Pₙ : ∀ n, CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R n)) ℤ)
      (b : ℤ)
      (uₙ : ∀ n, Pₙ (n + 1) ⟶
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (Pₙ n))
      (θₙ : ∀ n, ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (φ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (Pₙ (n + 1)) ≅ Pₙ n)
    (hbound : ∀ n, (Pₙ n).IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hterms : ∀ n i, Module.Free (R n) ((Pₙ n).X i) ∧
      Module.Finite (R n) ((Pₙ n).X i))
    (hsurju : ∀ n i, Function.Surjective ((uₙ n).f i))
    (hθₙ : ∀ n i, (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (φ n)).homEquiv
      ((Pₙ (n + 1)).X i) ((Pₙ n).X i) ((θₙ n).hom.f i) = (uₙ n).f i) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ)
      (p : ∀ n, P ⟶
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (Pₙ n))
      (θ : ∀ n, ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P ≅ Pₙ n),
      P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i, Module.Free A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Finite A (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ n i (y : P.X i), (uₙ n).f i ((p (n + 1)).f i y) = (p n).f i y) ∧
      (∀ i (x : ∀ n, (Pₙ n).X i), (∀ n, (uₙ n).f i (x (n + 1)) = x n) →
        ∃! y : P.X i, ∀ n, (p n).f i y = x n) ∧
      (∀ n i, (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (q n)).homEquiv
        (P.X i) ((Pₙ n).X i) ((θ n).hom.f i) = (p n).f i)
